chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When the woman initiates the mutual divorce (khula') with her husband, she is one of the parties initiating, and he is a suitor from among the suitors.

key_terms.بَارَأَتِ: To separate or divorce mutually, specifically khula where the wife initiates.
key_terms.خَاطِبٌ: Suitor or proposer (one who makes a proposal).
key_terms.وَاحِدَةٌ: One (implying the initiator or one of the two parties involved in the act).

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling when a wife initiates khula divorce against her husband?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Isfabar, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal dynamics of khula' by distinguishing the roles of the parties: the wife is the active initiator (bara'at) seeking separation, while the husband is likened to a suitor (khatab) who accepts the proposal. This metaphor underscores that although the husband's consent is necessary for the divorce to be finalized, the agency and primary intent rest with the wife, a key distinction in Shia fiqh regarding the validity and conditions of khula'.
